interaction.channel: CDP pointer input against both production Browser renderers
steps: Both renderers open the Terminal surface on the canonical seeded thread.
Both renderers receive the visible Split Terminal Horizontally pointer action.
Lynx keeps term-1 and term-2 simultaneously mounted at 269.5px each.
Lynx writes distinct markers through the shared command row after activating each pane.
Both pane transcripts retain only their own marker.
Closing term-2 restores term-1 as one full-width pane.

productLossClosed: Lynx now supports the Web authority horizontal split action rather than converting every new session into an exclusive tab.
Both live sessions remain visible, independently buffered, independently resized to half width, and selectable as the shared command target.
The first implementation rendered each Lynx pane at only 24px; strengthened geometry evidence found it and the product now renders two 269.5px panes.
missingCoverage: Native split correlation remains unavailable because Computer Use repeatedly resolves exact owned Lynxtron pid and window requests to unrelated same-bundle-id processes.
remainingProductResidual: Vertical split, more than two panes, xterm key-by-key behavior, and selection actions remain outside this slice.
acceptedRenderingNoise: Web labels its currently allocated sessions Terminal 2 and Terminal 3 while the isolated Lynx client labels its locally allocated sessions Terminal 1 and Terminal 2; both show the same two-pane lifecycle against the shared server.
classification.policy: No state weight, threshold, bad sample filter, or scope reduction was used.
